newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, outperform as dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, outperform as dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Friday, as spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowed on a stronger Canadian dollar and waning fears of a possible U.S. rate hike.

"The outperformance is really a response to the currency, which has found relief in the notion that the Fed won't have to do as much tightening," said Anita Lauria, a New York-based economist with Salomon Brothers.
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.42 to C$110.92 to yield 7.076 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 9/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at Thursday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets traded in a see-saw fashion on Friday. Bond markets were initially much stronger after the U.S. Labor Department reported the economy added 142,000 new jobs in April, below expectations of a 211,000 increase. However, the report also showed the jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent, the lowest in over 23 years.
Investors quickly pared bond market gains by selling to lock in profits on both the morning's gains and strong gains made during the past three sessions, analysts said.

But Canadian and U.S. bonds rebounded from negative territory later in the session on news that a U.S. budget accord had been reached. News of the accord, as well as lower-than-expected job growth, have combined to reduce expectations about the amount of tightening the Federal Reserve will undertake, analysts said. That, in turn, helped the Canadian dollar rally past C$1.3810 (US$0.7241).

"The movement of the Canadian dollar over the last 48 hours can be viewed as more of a relief trade since interest rate pressures from the U.S. have been relieved," Technical Data analyst David Ebata said in a commentary.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds rose C$0.35 to C$103.40 to yield 6.515 percent. The U.S. bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 15 basis points from 10 basis points on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.01 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.24 percent.
